subject: Learning Methods
title: The 90-Minute Sleep Cycle
description: A fast breakdown of The 90-Minute Sleep Cycle for builders.

hook.text: Waking up groggy often means your alarm hit mid-cycle. Waking between cycles feels dramatically more refreshing.

buildup.text: Each sleep cycle lasts roughly 90 minutes. Early cycles are deep-sleep heavy. Later cycles are REM heavy.

discovery.text: Planning sleep in 90-minute blocks means you wake at the lightest part of the cycle. Five cycles equals 7.5 hours.

twist.text: Individual cycle length varies from 80–120 minutes. Track your natural wake time for a week to find your personal.

climax.text: Count backward in 90-minute blocks from your wake time to find your ideal bedtime.

punchline.text: Sleep in full cycles. Wake between them. Feel refreshed.

quiz.question: Why does waking between sleep cycles feel more refreshing?
options: Between cycles, the body releases morning hormones
You wake from the lightest sleep phase instead of deep sleep
Cycle boundaries are when dreams end naturally
